inference_substrate_justification: The after row used live option-logit reads from the cached Qwen3.8-27B GGUF through CUDA llama.cpp. The placement-count measurement used the real local Tetris engine without an LLM.
reproducibility_checksum_scope: Canonical sorted JSON over model_specs, placement_count_measurement, overflow_fix, before_after, methodology, and source.
duration_measurement: Sum of the 67 client-reported request latencies. This excludes model hashing, model load, preflight, and short client-side gaps.

preconditions_checked.detail: Qwen3.8-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf resolved from the local Hugging Face cache
Set to 1 for preflight and server launch
4 MiB total and 0 MiB from other compute PIDs before load
llama_supports_gpu_offload returned true; server PID 582157 held 19738 MiB on physical GPU 1 and no compute allocation appeared on GPU 0
Both GPUs returned to 4 MiB and no compute process remained after shutdown

placement_count_measurement.percentile_method: Linear interpolation over the sorted 600 observed counts.
placement_count_measurement.interpretation: The 16-label cap affected most measured turns, so quality-independent truncation was a plausible material confound. This is a descriptive engine measurement, not an inferential population claim.

overflow_fix.policy: Rank placement evaluations before applying the 16-label cap.
overflow_fix.delegate_behavior: The delegate maps to the first placement in the remaining ranked tail.
overflow_fix.regression_fixture: A 20-placement fixture puts the best evaluation at raw-order p19. The exposed named list starts with p19, and the delegate targets ranked-tail p14.

before_after.comparison_type: Same model, seed, piece cap, composite mode, sum blend, and non-shuffled condition. The overflow ranking policy is the intended changed variable.
before_after.holes_comparison_note: The after run ended with two more holes only after surviving 39 more pieces. Final hole count alone is not a quality regression.

methodology.placement_measurement: Run the real engine for 300 pieces each at seeds 1 and 2. Select every move with heuristicPick and record enumeratePlacements(board, current).length before the move.
methodology.controls: No shuffle flag and no uniform flag. No second model or additional seed was run.

sample_size_note: The placement distribution has 600 turns across two deterministic heuristic games. The live before/after check has one pre-specified seed and supports only a targeted confound diagnosis, not a population effect or general model ranking.
surprising_result_acknowledgment: The 2.39 times survival increase is preliminary because the live comparison has one seed. It is not headline-eligible until replicated, but it is large enough to reject use of the first-pass seed-1 number as an overflow-unconfounded readout result.
plain_language_verdict: The ranking fix changed the seed-1 outcome meaningfully: survival rose from 28 to 67 pieces and lines rose from 0 to 17. This shows that the earlier stable-order truncation materially contributed to the poor result, so the first-pass numbers should not be trusted as a clean SemIf-versus-Tetris finding. The fix does not explain all weakness: the corrected run still topped out at 67 of 300 pieces, so the readout and policy still need harder evaluation.
claim_limits: One live seed cannot estimate an average treatment effect or establish a broad model claim.
The model inference is not deterministic enough to treat the difference as a perfectly controlled paired intervention.
The placement-count distribution came from heuristic-played boards, not the model's state distribution.
The corrected run still topped out, so this artifact does not claim parity with the keyword or El-Tetris baselines.
